podcast.title: Grammy Nomination - 2015
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran was nominated for Album of the Year at the 2015 Grammys, competing against Beck, Beyoncé, Sam Smith, and Pharrell Williams. "Beck won that Grammy in 2015, likely because he was old enough to be respectable and he was the token rock nominee in an album of the year ballot that also featured Beyonce, Ed Sheeran, Sam Smith, and Ferelle Williams."

podcast.title: Income Drop Despite New Material (2016)
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran experienced a significant drop in income in 2016, despite having released new material and touring that year. This illustrates that releasing new music alone may not always prevent an income decline if other factors are not aligned. "a pesar de haber sacado material sus ingresos han desplomado."

podcast.title: Apple Music Popularity - Second Spot
podcast.body: As of a recent check, Ed Sheeran was ranked as the second most listened-to artist on Apple Music, following Taylor Swift and preceding Drake. "The most listened to artists on Apple Music are Drake and number 3, Ed Sheeran in second spot, and Taylor Swift at number 1."

podcast.title: Contemporary British Chart Dominance
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran is among the "natives of Old Blighty" who are still capable of commanding the Hot 100 to this day, demonstrating continued UK incursions on the US charts beyond the 60s and 80s invasions. "From Adele to Ed Sheeran to Duolipa, natives of Old Blighty are still capable of commanding the Hot 100 to this day."

podcast.title: Copyright Infringement Cases
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran has been one of many prominent artists involved in copyright infringement controversies in the 2000s, alongside Coldplay, Led Zeppelin, Katy Perry, and Lady Gaga. "Ed Sheeran, Coldplay, Led Zeppelin, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga, and dozens more have all been wrapped up in these controversies."

podcast.body: Ed Sheeran is an example of an artist whose music heavily dominates the streaming medium, particularly within pop, R&B, and hip-hop genres. "You know, Drake, Ed Sheeran, the weekend, Justin Bieber."

podcast.title: Eclipsing U2's Tour Gross
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran is noted as one of the artists whose concert tours have surpassed the box office earnings of U2's 360 tour, highlighting his massive commercial success in the contemporary live music market. "Ed Sheeran, Elton John, Coldplay, and Taylor Swift have eclipsed that."

podcast.title: Global Success (End of 2010s)
podcast.body: This artist emerged from the growing UK folk scene to become one of the most successful solo performers globally by the end of the 2010s. "and of course Ed Sheeran, who would end up as one of the most successful solo performers in the world by the end of the decade."

podcast.title: Manager's Earnings & Touring Gross
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran's manager earned 30 million pounds in one year, which suggests Sheeran's own earnings were substantial, given managers typically take a 15-20% cut. Sheeran was also the third-highest-grossing touring act of the 2010s, bringing in $922 million. "Ed Sheeran's manager. His manager made 30 million pounds this year."

podcast.title: Sampling of Funky Drummer Break
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran is listed among the diverse artists who have sampled Clyde Stubblefield's drum break from James Brown's "Funky Drummer." "But also Ed Sheeran, Britney Spears, Nine Inch Nails, Kenny G, Stone Roses, Poppullet itself, and Shanato Conner."

podcast.title: Second Most Streamed Artist of the Decade (2010s)
podcast.body: Ed Sheeran was the second most streamed artist of the 2010s, demonstrating his significant global appeal and widespread adoption on streaming platforms. His high ranking underscores the massive shift in music consumption towards digital access. "Drake was the most streamed artist of the decade, followed by Ed Sheeran."

xref.title: Streaming Performance Compared to Pop Superstars
xref.body: Despite being one of the biggest rock acts of the last 30 years, the Foo Fighters were not considered "superstars" in terms of streaming. Their most streamed song, "Learn to Fly," had approximately 350 million listens by the end of the 2010s, a figure dwarfed by Ed Sheeran's "Shape of You" which garnered 2.4 billion streams. "But even for a band like The Food Fighters, one of the biggest rock acts of the last 30 years. It weren't superstars it's streaming."
